name: Neck Transition
description: Examines the color, texture, and geometric continuity across the face-to-neck boundary where face-swap models typically introduce visible seam artifacts and tonal mismatches.
mechanism:
This method analyzes the face-neck transition zone for deepfake detection:

1. **Transition Zone Identification**: The boundary region between the face (jaw, chin) and neck is identified. This transition zone is typically 20-50 pixels wide and is the most common artifact location for face-swap deepfakes.

2. **Gradient Analysis**: The image gradient across the transition zone is measured. Natural face-neck transitions show smooth, anatomically motivated gradients: skin color gradation, shadow from the mandible, and texture transition from facial skin to neck skin. Deepfake blending produces characteristic gradient anomalies — either over-smoothed (Poisson blending) or showing color steps.

3. **Rendering Quality Discontinuity**: The effective resolution and detail level on either side of the transition is compared. Generated faces may have different rendering quality than the original neck — different noise patterns, different compression artifacts, or different texture granularity. These quality discontinuities at the transition indicate compositing.

4. **Anatomical Transition Verification**: The face-neck transition should follow anatomical constraints: submental contour, hyoid region, sternocleidomastoid muscle visibility. The method checks whether surface geometry at the transition is anatomically correct. Deepfake blending may produce anatomically implausible neck-face junctions.

5. **Temporal Transition Tracking**: The transition zone characteristics are tracked across frames. Natural transitions remain anatomically consistent. Deepfake transitions may show varying artifact intensity — more visible at extreme head poses, during fast motion, or under challenging lighting — creating temporal variation in boundary quality.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through neck transition analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Li, Y. et al. (2020). Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection. CVPR.
Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
